answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying reputation to costly, verifiable work rather than free identities. Think of a terrace of trust: each level is earned only after an agent completes audited tasks, like tending a shared meadow where every contribution is visible and pruned if fake. A garden of peers then attests only to agents with a real history, so creating a thousand empty identities buys no trust, because trust grows slowly, is public, and cannot be copied.
